topIssues.title: kona-node: signer updates can be missed when watch notifications coalesce
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
Kona's signer update channel is `watch<Address>`, which retains only the latest value. A verifier that owns its current/previous signer state can therefore miss intermediate rotations when updates arrive before it consumes the channel.

For example, if L1 observation publishes A -> B -> C while gossip still knows A, gossip observes only A -> C. It retains A as the previous signer instead of B: blocks from B are rejected, and A can receive grace even though it is no longer the immediately previous signer. A -> B -> A can be invisible as an address change. Delayed consumption also means the verifier starts its grace timer later than the producer observed the rotation.

The normal rotation grace-period fix in https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23626 intentionally keeps the existing address channels and tracks grace locally in the verifier. This issue tracks the notification/history limitation separately; it does not block that fix.

Investigate ordered rotation notifications or publishing sufficient rotation state and observation time to make coalescing safe. Also distinguish channel coalescing from intermediate onchain rotations that occur between L1 state reads: fixing the channel alone cannot recover history the producer never observed.

Regression coverage should include A -> B -> C before consumption, A -> B -> A, and a delayed consumer that must not extend the intended grace window.

Related: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22839

topPRs.title: kona-sp1: update SP1 crypto patches to 6.10.0
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body:
Upgrades the SP1-patched crates the kona-sp1 guests use (the BLS12-381 and KZG crates, and the sha2, crypto-bigint, k256, p256 and substrate-bn patches) to the releases built for the SP1 version the SDK and zkVM already run. Before this, the guests ran patches built against older `sp1-lib` releases. The sha3 patch stays as it is: there is no newer release.

The EIP-2537 differential check inside the zkVM (`just check-bls12-381-zkvm`) passes all 1342 cases against revm's arkworks backend. Per-operation cycles are within 0.5% of before, except G1ADD (+8%) and G2ADD (+6%), a fixed cost per call. The ELF-gated estimate tests (`log_estimate_bounds_measured_pgu`, `consolidation_estimate_bounds_measured_pgu`) pass.
